passage:
Text 1
Some marine organisms, like jellyfish, can thrive in many different ocean environments. However, deep-sea coral species tend to be restricted in the types of habitats they can occupy. This is because many deep-sea coral species are only able to survive within very specific depth ranges. Over time, these species have likely become adapted to living under particular water pressure conditions. Therefore, these species struggle to survive at depths that have significantly higher or lower pressure than they are accustomed to.

Text 2
A recent study examined data from over 2,500 coral species to understand why deep-sea coral species occupy such narrow depth ranges. Researchers observed that when a coral species was found in an area with numerous other coral species, it typically inhabited much more limited depth zones. It is thus likely that competition for space and nutrients with other species, not water pressure, determines where these corals can establish themselves.
prompt: Based on the texts, both authors would most likely agree with which statement?

choices.A: Marine biologists have more advanced equipment for studying deep-sea corals than they had previously.
choices.B: Little is understood about how deep-sea corals reproduce in their natural environment.
choices.C: Deep-sea coral species are limited in where they can establish habitats.
choices.D: Deep-sea coral species that live at similar depths tend to have comparable lifespans.

explanation: Choice C is the best answer. Both texts state that deep-sea coral species have restricted habitats or narrow ranges, although they disagree on the reason for this limitation. Text 1 claims that water pressure adaptation is the main factor that determines where these corals can live, while Text 2 claims that competition with other species is the main factor. However, both texts agree that these corals are not able to thrive in many different environments.
